newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals futures end mixed, off lows.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals futures end mixed, off lows.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mixed Friday, after recovering from further weakness seen on the opening, but the three week downtrend still looks intact, analysts said.

"We saw fresh lows on the opening with spot gold dipping below $380, but fund shortcovering ahead of the end of the third quarter and bank buying helped provide support," Pell Brothers floor trader Don Tierney said.
COMEX December gold ended down 80 cents at $382.80, after recovering from an intraday low at $381.90 an ounce.

In New York bullion trade, spot gold closed quoted $380.15/380.65, dipping to a session low during the first hour of trade around $379.70. In London gold fixed at $380.70 Friday afternoon, up from $380.30 at the morning fix, but down from the New York close Thursday around $381.10.
The key support level at $380 that has held since early 1995 is still seen under threat next week though, traders said.
"Gold is clearly susceptible to further short selling, with a longer term target of $374," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
One month implied gold lease rates have been moving up, suggesting fresh short selling, analysts said.

Precious metals futures have been in a downtrend for the past three weeks, largely driven by fund selling, with investor demand low due to healthy U.S. stock and bond markets and low U.S. inflation, analysts said.
COMEX December silver ended up 3.5 cent at $4.920, after trading down to a session low at $4.855 early.

NYMEX October platinum ended down $2.00 an ounce at $385.80, after seeing a new low for the October contract at $385.50 early. In the spot market, platinum slipped to fresh two-and-a-half year lows at $382.75 Friday.
NYMEX December palladium ended up $1.00 though at $120.00.
-Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, +1-212-859-1641 email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
